name: v0.92.0 — Clearer Cost Receipts and Desktop Settings
body:
## Highlights

- **Clearer cost receipts.** Runs outside `serve` use OpenRouter's public price index. Exact model slugs get their own rates, and strict calls retain the quote used at admission. The `gpt-oss-20b` catalogue entry has also been refreshed. [#1305](https://github.com/brcampidelli/chimera-agent/pull/1305)
- **Easier-to-find Desktop settings.** Settings search finds the model-by-role routing table. Routing and receipt copy reads correctly in Brazilian Portuguese, and new conversations and answer-only turns show clearer status. [#1300](https://github.com/brcampidelli/chimera-agent/pull/1300)
- **Configurable planner.** Set `use_planner` on Kanban lanes, API runs, or workflow solve steps. The planner stays on by default. [#1301](https://github.com/brcampidelli/chimera-agent/pull/1301)

## Experiments

- **Memory extraction.** The benchmark was inconclusive. The 6,000-character cap and global model remain the defaults. An explicit extraction model and a deterministic pre-filter are opt-in. [#1303](https://github.com/brcampidelli/chimera-agent/pull/1303)
- **Cron model tiers.** The cheaper tier was fully correct on seven of eight synthetic jobs. The benchmark did not measure production jobs, and defaults are unchanged. [#1299](https://github.com/brcampidelli/chimera-agent/pull/1299)
- **Design refinement and proportionality.** The lean Design refinement and prompt proportionality experiments remain off by default. [#1304](https://github.com/brcampidelli/chimera-agent/pull/1304) · [#1302](https://github.com/brcampidelli/chimera-agent/pull/1302)

Desktop installers are unsigned and may prompt on first launch. The app verifies signatures on updater bundles.

name: v0.91.0
body:
### Added

- **A conversation warns when its prompt cache stops working, and Worth shows the cost per resolved run.** When the share of prompt tokens read from cache falls below 80% across the turns whose route reports cache, the turn receipt and status bar say so once, with the main cause, and rearm when it recovers; a route that reports no cache never warns. Worth gains US$ per resolved run (all runs' cost over the ones that passed), the same per verifier-confirmed run, and the share of runs with a known price; it shows "—" when any run has no price, and stays sorted by name, not ranked. (P1-10, slices d and e) (#1288)

- **`chimera models` and Settings list every role's model, effort and origin.** `GET /api/routing` answers which model each role runs on, at which effort, where that choice came from, and whether the effort is sent on that route. What leaves through it is sanitised: a local path shows only its file name, a URL loses its user, password and query, and a denied provider's message is cleaned the same way. (P1-10, slice b) (#1294)

- **Reasoning effort per role.** `CHIMERA_ROLE_EFFORTS` sets the reasoning effort of the code roles and of the fusion cast, and an agent file's `effort: low|medium|high` now applies to that subagent's own calls. A repository's agent file cannot raise the effort the owner chose. (P1-10, slice c) (#1292)

- **A scheduled job can name its own model, effort and step budget, and sees its last delivery.** `cron add/edit --model --effort --max-steps` and the Schedule screen set them (empty inherits from `serve`, as before); invalid values are refused at save and, for a hand-edited `jobs.json`, inherited with a warning instead of dropping the job. The job's last delivered answer (2 KB, fenced as data) closes its context so it stops repeating itself; a delivery the destination refused counts toward the failure brake and is never treated as delivered. A webhook job naming these fields is refused. (P1-03) (#1287)

- **One table says which model each role runs on, and why.** `Settings.routing_table()` reports, per role, the model and the reasoning effort and where each came from (environment, `.env` or saved setting, product default). It reads the existing resolvers and changes no behaviour: a 432-case matrix, pinned as a snapshot, matches the old functions, and a ratchet keeps new `*_model` reads from spreading outside it. (P1-10, slice a) (#1286)

### Changed

- **Governance starts in `observe` on a new data folder.** A folder that is missing or empty gets `observe` once, recorded in `governance_default.json`; an existing folder keeps `off` and gets a notice (in the log at the start of `serve`/the app, and a dismissible note in Settings). An explicit `CHIMERA_GOVERNANCE` still wins, and an empty one counts as unset. Behaviour change: under `observe` the kernel's fixed hard blocks (`rm -rf /`, `mkfs`, curl into a shell, ...) refuse, so a new install now refuses those commands; what `enforce` would only send to review is recorded, not asked. (P0-15, part 2) (#1289)

### Fixed

- **The Chrome extension holds Stop, checks where a navigation goes before it is sent, and shows only the buttons that apply.** Stop survives a service-worker or Chrome restart until you press Start, and cancels an operation already under way; a Chimera tab opens blank and is protected before any URL loads, and each top-level navigation (redirects and history included) is checked against the sites you allowed before the request leaves. Typing into a field a page calls a search box asks for a card. The popup no longer shows Allow and Resume when there is nothing to allow or resume. Chrome 125 or newer is required. Known limit: a popup the page opens (`window.open`, `target=_blank`) can send its first request before the extension sees it; see docs/chrome-extension.md. (P1-20) (#1295)

- **An MCP server whose code changed under the same tool listing is held before it starts.** A change to its package version, script, module, executable or load-affecting environment now holds the server for approval ("command changed"); a pin from before this check is held once to record its identity, and the MCP screen says what could not be verified offline. Untrusted text in Code turns, the CI fix turn, the reviewer evidence and the quarantined reader now share one data fence, and the affective self-claim check covers Portuguese. (P1-12) (#1291)

- **A guest of a shared conversation sees the answers, not the owner's workings.** Live, on replay and in the model's own context, a guest no longer receives the tool arguments and results, edit diffs, approval previews, browser pictures, verifier output, instruction sources, cost receipts or host paths of the owner's turns: only the answers and the tool names and status, through an allowlist that drops any frame type it does not know. (#1293)

- **Screen readers hear a failed turn as failed, and keyboard focus shows where it is.** A turn that ends in an error is announced as "Failed: <reason>", never as complete; the conversation announces working, waiting and complete instead of reading the answer token by token; an approval that pauses the agent is announced once, not again after minimising and reopening it; and focus is visible on the settings tab panels, the Connections fields, the file editor and the command palette. (P1-20) (#1290)

name: v0.90.0
body:
### Added

- **`chimera report governance` and a governed `chimera agent`.** The report counts, per surface over the last N days, what governance granted, refused, raised to review and withheld, and under `observe` what `enforce` would have refused or put before an approver. `chimera agent` now runs on the same governed assembly as chat, assist and tui, so its hooks come from the project it works in and `--deny-tools` reaches deferred MCP tools. (#1283)

- **Claude 5 models in the catalogue, priced and asked only what they accept.** Fable 5.2, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 carry verified prices (Haiku 5.5's long-context tier included); the gateway stops sending parameters a model refuses; an exact provider cost is never rebuilt below what was spent, and an unknown one stays unpriced so the spend cap still holds. Fable 5.2's data-retention requirement is shown in the privacy card and the security docs. (#1279)

- **The Storage card now sees the conversations' worktrees, says why each is kept, and offers to archive idle ones.** It used to list only the worktrees in the system temp folder, missing the project's durable folder (89 checkouts, 72.9 GiB measured on one machine); it now lists them with size, age and the reason each still exists, warns above a limit (`CHIMERA_WORKTREE_LIMIT_GB`, default 50) and offers to archive conversations idle for `CHIMERA_WORKTREE_IDLE_DAYS` (default 14) through the existing archive route, never deleting anything. A new worktree card also says "fetching the remote base" while it waits and highlights the warning when it did not start from the remote tip. (P1-18) (#1253)

- **Token and cost baseline, read-only.** `scripts/token_baseline.py` reads the usage, run and trace logs under the desktop home and prints only aggregates (per surface, with coverage of price and cache and a 30-turn floor below which only the n is shown); its totals match the Cost screen over the same rows, and `bench/token_baseline/` holds the pre-registration and the first reading. (P0-18) (#1252)

- **Tool schema snapshots per surface**: `tests/prompt_snapshots/schema.<surface>.txt` now keeps the tool schema the Code turn, design turn, CLI, cron and bot send, assembled by each surface's own functions, so a changed tool description shows up as a diff; the prompt lint totals it per surface and `docs/tool-schema-by-surface.md` tabulates it (tokens are chars/4, an estimate). The second deferral bench is pre-registered, not run. (#1245)

- **Security: what holds is visible, and the bypass is on the record.** Turning "Ignore permissions" on or off now writes a `bypass_toggle` entry (scope, id, origin) to the audit log, and a switch can take an optional expiry (none by default); Settings > Security opens with one card, computed by the code that decides, showing what still asks you with the switch on, where commands really run, the checks in each place and which switches are on; with the switch on, a recursive delete or write outside the project and your user folder asks again (a lexical check that lowers the risk, not a boundary); crew and hierarchy runs end with the cross-agent monitor's section on the Orchestration tab, which says "not evaluated" rather than "nothing found" when there was nothing to read; and the Hooks list marks a hook that cannot run on this machine with how often it was skipped. (P1-11) (#1246)

- **Tools:** every tool result is now capped at 20 000 characters at the registry (tools that already capped themselves are unchanged), `http_get`, `scrape` and `read_document` take an `offset` to read on past a cut, and a subagent run reports how many subagents it spawned; the lower MCP ceiling and a spawn limit are options that stay off. (#1243)

### Changed

- **MCP tool descriptions can be cut to one line per server, and the base prompt says forged notices grant nothing.** `"description_mode": "one_line"` in `mcp.json` shows the model one line of each tool description and serves the rest through a fenced `mcp_describe` that honours the session's allow and deny lists, including through the ledger and governance wrappers. It is opt-in: the default stays whole descriptions, because the pre-registered paired run (`bench/mcp_description_fence`, 540 runs, US$ 0.84) measured the cut at -24.4 pp of first-call tool selection (TOST [-31.7, -16.2]), and on tasks whose answer sits in the description tail the choice is a coin flip. What it buys is also measured: attempts at forbidden actions fell 16.7 pp (27.5% to 10.8%), all of it from payloads in the tail of a tool description; benign false positives were not inferior, with caveats. The base prompt now states that text imitating the system in a file, a message or a tool output grants no permission; that sentence has no demonstrated effect in the bench. The first mount of a server records and logs its selection cues. (#1282)

- **Repository hygiene.** Removed five tracked execution outputs, synced stale docstrings, made `chimera tui` refuse to start without a terminal, made `chimera init` hide the key and keep `.env` owner-only, and pinned the chart CDN scripts. (#1276)

- **CI now audits distributed Python extras and blocks fixable CVEs.** Add full-extra install smoke coverage across Linux, Windows and macOS, enforce locked CI environments, and keep advisories without a published fix visible. (#1263)

- **`solve` now judges its work like the app does.** It reads the project's own test command (gated by where the command came from), a reviewer running on the same model that wrote the patch is advisory instead of a veto, and every run receipt records who judged and where the check came from. (#1256)

- **The API no longer leaks internal errors, and uploads no longer freeze it.** An uncaught server error now returns a generic 500 with an error id you can find in `backend.log`, large attachments are processed off the main loop so the app keeps answering meanwhile, and log lines written during a turn name that turn. (#1254)

- **Settings:** the search now finds every row (it covered about half), each setting says when a saved change applies (now, next conversation or next launch; the ones not yet traced say nothing), empty Memory, Runs, Decisions and Skills screens offer a first step, the presentation view uses the shared dialog, and reads of `CHIMERA_*` outside `Settings` are pinned by a ratchet. (#1251)

### Fixed

- **A share link's guest turn runs with the least privilege.** It no longer reaches the owner's other conversations, mailbox, calendar, skill bundles, MCP servers, global instructions, hooks, browser sign-ins, lessons or other conversations' jobs; it has no shell, runs nothing it could have edited (verifier, formatter, hooks, git), and cannot read or write outside the conversation's folder or inside Chimera's own data, even through symlinks, junctions or instruction imports. Rendered PNG/SVG charts now refuse remote data URLs, and snapshots no longer follow links out of the workspace, for everyone. (#1281)

- **The Design check measures HTML artboards.** Colours, fonts, spacing and text contrast are checked against the tokens, and anything the check could not measure is listed as "not checked" instead of reading as "no findings". (#1277)

- **The app's agent now knows who you are.** The profile you fill in (stored profile and remembered facts about you) is added to the agent's instructions in the same place in the desktop Code turn, the terminal and the bots, and stays identical between turns so prompt caching keeps working. (#1275)

- **Pasted credentials no longer sit in chat session files, and a web page can no longer POST to a token-less local server.** Chat transcripts are masked on disk, writes from another origin are refused when no server token is set, the attachment and dictation uploads get the same origin check as skill uploads, and a non-ASCII bearer header now gets a 401 instead of a 500. (#1274)

- **A retry after a failed verification now really escalates.** It raises the reasoning effort, then moves to the next single model, instead of rerunning the same model while the receipt claimed fusion; fusion no longer joins any turn that carries tools, including "fuse this turn", and each attempt in the receipt records the model and effort actually sent. (#1272)

- **Memory recall no longer drops facts written in Russian, Chinese or Japanese.** The admission gate used an ASCII-only word splitter, so a fact that recall had just found was discarded as "irrelevant" without any message; it now reads text the same way recall does, and the code search index follows suit. (#1271)

- **Safer release pipeline.** Every CI action is pinned to a commit, PyPI publishing now refuses a manual run off `main` or a tag that differs from the package version, and the Docker image runs as a non-root user. (#1262)

- **"Ignore permissions" no longer releases what its own floor keeps for you.** With the switch on, a force push to `main`, `git push origin +main`, an upload of `.env` and `powershell -EncodedCommand` were refused by the floor and then approved by the card one step later; every surface now applies one rule, and the GitHub, Azure, Docker and Kubernetes CLI credential files are refused by the bridge, the switch and the SSH file tools alike. (#1261)

- **Cost numbers now agree.** The Cost screen shows the real cache hit rate (it was capped at 50%), the daily spend cap counts autonomous `solve` runs and the blog writer like the screen does, and only one cron daemon runs per home so a scheduled job no longer fires twice when the app and `chimera serve --cron` are both open. (#1260)

- **Keyboard focus is now easy to see.** The focus ring is a solid outline that reaches 3:1 against every surface in every theme and accent, gets thicker in High contrast and stays visible in Windows High Contrast, and tabs now correctly name the panels they control for screen readers. (#1258)

- **Links in a reply can no longer carry the app's credentials away.** The desktop window now stays on its own pages (other sites open in your browser), and the access tokens it holds are given only to the app itself, never to a site it is sent to or to the dev-server and Design previews inside it. (#1259)

- **Memory you can see and trust.** The turn receipt now lists the facts a reply used, with where each came from and an unverified mark, and lets you forget one on the spot; the Memory screen flags near-duplicate facts written on different days so you can keep the right one, and tidying memory no longer risks losing facts or paying for the same merge twice. (#1257)

- **Every HTML page the server hands out now carries a Content-Security-Policy.** FastAPI's `/redoc` and `/docs/oauth2-redirect`, served outside the token guard with no policy and loading a CDN script onto the app's origin, are off; `/api/docs` sends a policy naming exactly what Swagger loads; a stray `.htm` or `.xhtml` at the bundle root is policed like `.html`; and a new test requests every page and enumerates every route outside the API so the next one cannot ship without a policy. (#1248)

- **Two tests that depended on timing now measure what they claim.** The shared-conversation test waits for the animation frame that draws streamed tokens since #1247, and the pathological-command test warms the shell parser up before starting its 1 s clock; both limits are unchanged. (#1250)

- **Faster CLI start, and a repo that searches better.** `chimera --help` no longer imports the agent core, the Discord adapter or `httpx` (`chimera code` took three names from `chimera.server.desktop_mcp`, whose package `__init__` loads the whole server stack; they now live in the stdlib-only `chimera/api/bridge_transport.py`, re-exported under the old names), and `chimera version` drops from 1.16 s to about 0.78 s in a back-to-back median on the same machine, the rest being `chimera.config`. A `.rgignore` hides bench data and generated files from ripgrep (a closed, commented list; `PREREGISTRATION*`, `RESULT*` and sources stay searchable), `bench/INDEX.md` lists every bench directory with a status read from its files, and installing with `uv tool install chimera-agent` or `pipx install chimera-agent` is documented; `install.sh` now says which Python version it needs. The paired benchmark that would measure the `.rgignore` is pre-registered in `bench/rgignore_context/` and not yet run. (P1-16) (#1249)

- **Desktop: streaming no longer re-renders the whole conversation per token.** Finished exchanges are memoised, streamed text is written once per frame, the heavy screens (Settings, Knowledge, Automation, Work, Onboarding, Activity) and the syntax highlighter load on demand, the running-turns poll is a single hook, and on-screen clocks pause while the window is hidden. Auto-detected highlighting now chooses among the 14 languages the file viewer maps. Not yet measured in the packaged app (see `apps/desktop/PROFILING.md`). (#1247)

- **TUI: unknown slash commands and `/undo N`.** The full-screen terminal app no longer sends an unrecognised `/command` to the model as a paid turn, `/undo N` now previews and asks before restoring, and `chat`, `assist` and the TUI build their command lists from one shared registry. (#1242)

name: v0.89.0
body:
### Fixed

- **The "Plan first" choice survives a reload.** Auto, Always or Never in the Code composer is now remembered per conversation, and a new conversation starts at the last choice made; before, reloading the window put it back on Auto. A test also pins that a plan waiting for approval, and its card, come back after a reload. (#1239)

- **Settings search finds the Environments card.** "WSL", "SSH" or "environment" in the Settings search now lists the Environments card and the allowed SSH hosts, and opening a result scrolls to it; before, the card was on the General tab but the search could not find it. (#1236)

### Added

- **File tools work on the SSH host.** In an SSH conversation, reading, writing, editing, patching, listing, grep and glob now act on the remote folder instead of refusing. Paths cannot leave the conversation's folder (checked lexically and with the host's own realpath, so a symlink cannot escape), credential files such as `.ssh`, `.env`, keys and cloud configs are refused, a write is replaced only after its size and hash are checked on the host, the Manual card shows the diff of the remote file and names the host, and in a turn that read outside content a write to a git hook, shell startup file, cron or systemd asks first. What the host returns counts as outside content. (#1240)

- **SSH commands survive a dropped connection.** In an SSH conversation each command now runs detached on the remote host under its own run id; if the link drops, Chimera reconnects and keeps reading the output without starting the command again. A script that arrives incomplete is never run, a timeout or Stop ends the whole process group, and if Chimera closes mid-command the command keeps running and the conversation that started it is told where its output is. (#1238)

- **Act on many folders or conversations at once.** The Folders card in Settings and the Code sidebar gain checkboxes, a tri-state "Select all" and an action bar: pin, unpin, allow or revoke commands, remove from the lists or show again for folders; archive, unarchive, delete or remove their folders from the lists for conversations. Selection mode draws every row so nothing off screen is acted on, deleting asks first with the count, allowing commands in bulk asks first, and one failure is counted without stopping the rest. (#1237)

name: v0.88.0
body:
### Fixed

- **The plan panel's Approve and Ask for changes answer the right question.** The plan event now carries the id of the approval it waits on, and the panel offers its buttons only when that id matches the approval pending on the card; before, it matched by text. A plan whose approval it cannot identify shows "waiting for approval on the card" with no buttons, instead of saying it was approved. (#1233)

- **Settings search finds the hooks and worktree cleanup switches.** Typing "hook" or "worktree" in the Settings search now lists the lifecycle hooks, the Claude Code hook switches and the archived-worktree cleanup, and opening a result focuses its switch; before, these rows were on the General tab but the search could not find them. (#1229)

### Added

- **Run a conversation's commands on another machine over SSH.** A saved environment can now be an SSH host: an alias from your `~/.ssh/config` that you added to the allowed hosts in Settings, plus the remote folder commands run in. Commands go through your system's `ssh` with your agent and `known_hosts`, never a password or key typed into Chimera; a new or changed host key is never accepted on its own, agent and port forwarding are off, and the config cannot turn a command into a different one. A dropped connection is retried only when the client log shows the command never started, so nothing runs twice. The local file tools are off in an SSH conversation so the agent cannot edit the wrong machine; files on the host are reached through commands for now. SSH counts as running on the host for the host-exec gate and the permission modes, a turn that read outside content asks before each SSH command, and only your own screen manages hosts and environments. (#1234)

- **Choose where a conversation's commands run: on this machine or in WSL.** Before the first message, the Code screen offers the saved environments (Settings lists, adds and removes them; a WSL one names a distribution) and a project can have a default; after the first turn the environment is fixed, and a removed one leaves the conversation without commands rather than falling back to this machine. In WSL, `run_shell` and `execute_code` run through `wsl.exe --exec bash -lc` in the same folder seen as `/mnt/<drive>/...`, while file tools stay on this disk. WSL is not isolation: it counts as running on the host for the host-exec gate, Manual and Accept edits, and it is refused when the install is set to an isolated sandbox. The paths it can reach are read back as Windows paths by the fences that guard the audit log, the approvals queue, `.env`, MCP tokens and hooks, so `/mnt/c/...`, `cd` chains and `-C DIR` cannot get around them. Only your own screen creates, removes or chooses an environment. (#1232)
- **The receipt says why a turn missed the cache, and an idle conversation sends a shorter history.** A Code turn that read nothing from the prompt cache now names the cause: first turn, the cache's lifetime ran out during a pause, the system prompt or the tools changed, the model or route changed, or the route has no explicit cache; the status bar shows the last cause. When a conversation sat idle past its provider's cache lifetime (five minutes on Anthropic; nothing is assumed for other providers), the next turn sends a compacted history through the agent's own compaction, since the full history would be paid at full price anyway. Only what is sent is shortened: the stored conversation and what you see stay complete. A summary that calls a model counts toward the turn's budget and appears on the receipt, a conversation that read outside content is compacted without a model summary, and a failure here never stops the turn. `CHIMERA_IDLE_COMPACTION`, on by default. (#1231)

- **Scheduled tasks: missed runs, history, a permission mode and a worktree per task.** A task whose time passed while the app was off runs once when it is back, if the missed time is at most 7 days old, never once per missed time (`catch_up`: once or skip; a pause shorter than 30 minutes is not a miss). Every scheduled time is recorded with whether it ran and why not, shown per task on the Schedule screen. A task can have one of the Code screen's permission modes, never wider than Settings and never "Ignore permissions"; a mode that would ask someone refuses instead, and only your own screen sets it. A task can run in a fresh worktree, removed afterwards only when it left nothing (no changes, no ignored files, no unpushed commit), otherwise kept with its path in the history. (#1230)

name: v0.87.0
body:
### Added

- **Claude Code's instruction files reach the run.** Beside `AGENTS.md`, Chimera now reads `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `CLAUDE.local.md`, with their `@file` imports (`CHIMERA_CLAUDE_COMPAT`, on by default), and the Context card names the files a turn was given. Your personal `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` joins only your own surfaces, the CLI chat and code and the desktop Code turn, never a bot, webhook, scheduled job, subagent or shared-link guest, and it has its own budget. Imports stay inside the folder they belong to, are capped in size and count, and are re-read when their content changes. Prompt snapshots and benchmarks pin the switch off so they do not depend on the machine. (#1221)

- **`.worktreeinclude`, and archived worktrees cleaned up.** A new conversation worktree can copy the ignored files the project's `.worktreeinclude` names, such as `.env`, once you consent for that project and that version of the file; the consent shows which files it selects, and a new matching file asks again. Each copy is checked to be ignored inside the worktree, links are rechecked right before copying, and listing stops after 20 seconds and says so. The worktree of a conversation archived for 30 days is then removed (`CHIMERA_WORKTREE_CLEANUP`, on by default), but only when its tree is clean, everything is pushed and no ignored file is left that `.worktreeinclude` did not copy, so it can always be recovered from the remote branch; the sweep never forces a removal or deletes an unmerged branch, and keeps a folder another conversation still uses. (#1220)
- **Claude Code hooks, and they can only tighten.** Hooks in a project's `.claude/settings.json` and `.claude/settings.local.json`, and in your `~/.claude/settings.json`, run through Chimera's hook runner for PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SubagentStop, SessionStart, Notification and PreCompact, and Settings lists them with their origin. A hook can refuse or narrow a call, never widen it: `allow` means "no objection" and a rewritten input applies only if it narrows. A project's hooks never run on your machine, only in the sandbox with the network off, and only after you trust that exact version from your own screen; a change to the file, or to a file the command names, asks again. The file tools may not write `.claude/settings*.json`. Switches `CHIMERA_CLAUDE_HOOKS_REPO` and `CHIMERA_CLAUDE_HOOKS_USER` are on by default and owner-only; running your own hooks on the host needs a separate switch, off by default. (#1223)

- **`/skill-doctor`: what your skills cost.** `/skill-doctor` on the Code screen, or `chimera skills doctor` in the CLI, lists every skill a run is told about with its estimated context cost on each turn, its origin, how often it was used and a suggestion, such as a learned card nobody uses. It only reports; switching a skill off is still a click on the Skills screen. (#1222)

- **Select an element in the preview and send it to the agent.** "Select element" in the Preview panel (or Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+S) shows a picture of the dev server's page; a click on it puts the element in the composer as chips, its tag and text plus a crop. It runs in Chimera's own browser with a throwaway cookie profile, injects no script into the project's page, only reaches the conversation's own dev server, and refuses the pick if the page changed since the picture. What comes from the page is outside content: the text and the crop both taint the turn. (#1218)

- **Claude Code subagents work in Chimera.** Agents written for Claude Code in `.claude/agents` (up to the repository root), `~/.claude/agents` and plugins are listed beside `.chimera/agents`, with their origin, role and memory shown on the Agents screen. A file can only narrow what it gets: its tools are intersected with the session's governed tools, `permissionMode` can only restrict, `bypassPermissions` is ignored with a warning, and a model name such as `opus` maps to a role the owner sets in Settings. An agent with memory keeps fenced notes through scoped Read/Write/Edit, and notes that come from the repository are treated as untrusted when the workspace isn't trusted. (#1219)

- **Dev-server preview with auto-verify on the Code screen.** `.chimera/launch.json` (or `.claude/launch.json`) names the project's dev servers; the preview panel starts and stops them, shows their log and frames the page, and the agent's `preview` tool can start one, take a screenshot and read the console. Starting a server is running a command, so it goes through the same `run_shell` path — sandbox, governance, deny list, taint, the Manual card — and the panel's own button is checked against the hard blocks too. Before answering, a turn that changed front-end files checks the page and is not reported verified while the console shows errors; it never starts a server after reading outside content or after the launch file, `package.json` or a config file changed in that turn. Only ports a server of the turn actually listens on are reachable, the app's own ports never are, and the frame runs without same-origin access. (#1217)

- **`/code-review` on the Code screen.** It reviews the conversation's changes (the git diff, or the conversation's own edits when there is no repository) with a model that has no tools, and returns a card grouped by file: severity, file and line, "Show in diff" (scrolls to the line) and "Apply fixes" for the findings you tick. The diff is treated as outside content, so the conversation is marked tainted and applying fixes asks first; findings the verifier did not check are labelled and left unticked; the review has a size, batch and time budget and says what it left out; and it only reviews the conversation's own folder. (#1214)

- **A plan panel on the Code screen.** When a turn proposes a plan, the panel lists its steps and, while the plan waits for you, offers Approve and Ask for changes through the same approval the card uses, so answering in one place answers in both. It shows only the latest turn's plan, says when the turn is waiting on the card even after a reload, and announces the decision you sent until the turn finishes. (#1213)

### Changed

- **Manual mode now asks before every edit and every command.** Each file write — editing, patching, charts, downloads, generated media, design exports — and each command shows a card first (with the proposed diff for text edits): allow once, allow editing that file or running that exact command for this conversation, or refuse. Reading never asks; a turn with no screen (bots, schedules, background work, the bridge) is refused at once instead of waiting; Manual ignores old project-wide "always allow" rules and the allow approval mode; and only the owner's screen can grant "for this conversation". One table now names every tool that writes to the workspace, read by the ledger, the read-only posture and Manual alike. (#1215)

name: v0.86.0
body:
### Added

- **Conversations archive themselves when their pull request is merged or closed (on by default).** A background sweep, at most once a minute, archives a conversation whose recorded pull request changes to merged or closed, and stores why; it never archives one with a turn running, a question or approval waiting, background work or a share link, it does not re-archive a conversation you brought back for the same pull request, and it deletes nothing. A GitHub login or network failure pauses the sweep for ten minutes; a problem with one pull request only skips that conversation. Turn it off in Settings › General › Autonomy. (#1205)

- **One mode picker under the prompt (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+M): Manual, Accept edits, Plan, Auto, Don't ask, and Ignore permissions when the project allows it.** Each mode maps onto the existing posture instead of adding a third mechanism; the conversation's mode is saved and starts from what Settings say (never → Don't ask, suspicious → Auto, always → Manual). Accept edits shows a card before each command unless it only reads or the sandbox isolates it, and Plan never runs wider than Auto. The bridge can only move a conversation to a mode that widens nothing. Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+O opens the model picker and Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+E the effort picker; maximise moved to Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Enter. (#1207)

- **Comment on diff lines and send them all to the agent at once.** In the Code screen's diffs, a "+" beside each line opens a comment box; Enter keeps the comment on that line, and "Send comments (N)" or Ctrl/Cmd+Enter sends every pending comment as one message with file, line, the line's text and which diff it came from. Comments are kept per conversation until they are sent, a comment from an older edit is marked as possibly out of date, and the rows are keyboard-navigable. (#1203)

- **The agent's shell no longer receives your API keys.** Child processes of the agent (and the new terminal) used to inherit provider key pools such as `CHIMERA_OPENROUTER_KEYS`, `DATABASE_URL` with a password and cloud credentials, so any command the agent ran could print them. They now get an environment with secrets removed by name and by value (proxy settings still pass), while the GitHub CLI keeps the token it needs. (#1208)

- **A real terminal in the Code screen (Ctrl+`).** Tabs (up to eight) open a real shell in the conversation's folder or worktree, so `cd`, `export` and interactive programs work. Only the desktop app's own screen opens one: the bridge, paired browser tabs and devices, chat bots and guests cannot, a folder whose commands are off has no terminal, and nothing typed is logged. Closing a tab, the conversation or the app ends the shell and everything it started (a job object on Windows).

- **Side chat (Ctrl/Cmd+;) for a quick question about the conversation without adding to it.** It reads the conversation as data, answers with no tools, and writes nothing into the conversation's history; "Bring into the conversation" only fills the composer, and when the conversation has read outside content it quotes the answer as data and asks first. Its cost is recorded (an interrupted answer as an estimate), local models stay free under a daily cap, and the shortcuts help moved to Ctrl/Cmd+/. (#1204)

- **Suggested-task cards: the agent proposes side work instead of drifting into it.** When it notices something outside the task (dead code, a stale doc, a missing test, a security issue seen in passing) it can only propose a card; you see the full prompt before anything runs and choose Start (a new conversation in the same project), Do it here, Options or Dismiss, with Start all asking for confirmation and capped at five. Only the owner's screen starts a card, the server keeps the prompt (the page sends only the card id), and a card proposed by a turn that read outside content starts its conversation marked as tainted and without "Ignore permissions", with a warning on the card. (#1206)

### Changed

- **Reversible features now start on.** Closing the loop on a verified Code turn (commit, open the pull request, follow the CI and run up to two fix turns), pull requests, bots transcribing voice notes locally, and deferred tools are on by default; merging stays off and has its own owner-only switch, and billing, destructive migrations, row-level security, grants and secrets still never merge by themselves. Skill cards stay off, now with the revised measurement on screen (+37–48% tokens, and −8.3 pp in a repeat run). A deferred tool is only loaded later, never granted: the owner's policy, the project pack and the posture are checked again when it is called, a subagent is never handed a denied one, and calling a harmless deferred tool no longer marks the turn as tainted. Benchmarks pin the old defaults so their published numbers still reproduce. (#1210)

### Fixed

- **The catalogue no longer promises a 128k window for Mistral Small 3.2.** OpenRouter now serves it with 32,768 tokens of context, which the live check on main caught; the row now says 32k, so context sizing and the model picker stop overestimating it. (#1211)

- **The desktop app no longer hands the backend its secrets through the environment.** The server token, the screen credential and the launcher key used to travel as environment variables, which on Linux stay readable in `/proc/<pid>/environ` to any process of the same user, the agent's shell included. They now arrive on the backend's stdin as one line that is read and closed; the server token is kept in memory rather than in the process environment; a missing or malformed line stops the backend instead of starting it without a token; and the app refuses to use a backend that answers without one. (#1209)

name: v0.85.0
body:
### Fixed

- **A run whose child process keeps its output pipe open no longer hangs.** Streaming a command's output used to wait without limit for the pipe to close, so a grandchild that inherited it (a test runner's worker, a background server) kept the run, its cancel button and the test suite waiting forever. The reader now runs on its own thread with a five-second grace after the child exits, cancelling kills the whole process group on POSIX and the process tree on Windows, and the test suite dumps every thread's stack if a single test runs past fifteen minutes instead of freezing silently. (#1196)

- **The settings search finds the pull-request and close-the-loop switches.** Searching "pull request", "PR", "merge", "close the loop" (or "ciclo" in Portuguese) now lands on and focuses those two switches, and "autonomia" finds the card that holds them, in every language the app offers. Before, the search found nothing and the new close-the-loop switch could only be reached by scrolling. (#1193)

### Changed

- **Design artboards and their exports load images from `data:` only.** The content security policy of an artboard, and of the HTML it exports, no longer allows `blob:` images; every other directive is unchanged, so the policy only got stricter. Nothing the app builds used `blob:` (assets already arrive as `data:` URLs), and no existing design referenced one. (#1194)

### Added

- **A browser tab can become the owner's screen by pairing with a one-time code.** The desktop app shows an eight-character code (five minutes, five attempts); typing it into the browser grants that tab an HttpOnly, same-site cookie for up to twelve hours, revocable from the desktop. Only the desktop issues codes — the bridge and the chat channels cannot — and a paired tab cannot turn on the bridge, full control or "Ignore permissions". Every state-changing request from it must come from the same origin. (#1198)

- **Discord and Telegram bots can hear voice messages and answer aloud, locally.** Voice notes are transcribed on this machine with faster-whisper (pinned model revision, duration checked before decoding, a per-user rate limit). Spoken replies are off by default and use Piper only when the owner points `CHIMERA_CHAT_VOICE_MODEL` at a voice `.onnx` they chose; Chimera ships no voice, and `piper-tts` (GPL-3.0) lives in a separate `voice` extra outside `[full]`. (#1197)

- **Named OpenAI-compatible endpoints from Settings.** Settings › Connections now lists your OpenAI-compatible endpoints (a local vLLM, LM Studio or llama.cpp server, or a hosted one) and lets you add, test and remove them; the test makes one bounded `GET /models` call to that endpoint only. Only the owner's screen can change or test them, the key is never shown, and an endpoint's key must be its own `*_API_KEY` variable, never another provider's credential or a `CHIMERA_` setting. Closes #1133. (#1195)

name: v0.84.0
body:
### Added

- **Code-screen turns record lessons, and the minting gates are real.** A finished Code turn now records a short lesson in its own store (`code_lessons.json`), which only the Code screen reads and only with skill cards on; the setting stays off by default, because seven pre-registered runs found no gain from learning, and autonomous runs never see these lessons. An unchecked answer is recorded as unverified rather than as a success, background and tainted work are kept out of the prompt, and the text is capped. Every minting path now names its trace, so its cards are no longer refused for lack of evidence, and a recurrence now needs two shared content words, in Portuguese too, instead of one. (#1191)

- **A finished turn can commit, open its PR and follow the CI (off by default).** With "Close the loop" on in Settings, a Code-screen turn that passed verification and its own diff check commits on its worktree branch, pushes it, opens a pull request and watches the CI in the background; a red CI is read and up to two fix turns follow, and a green one merges. A pull request that touches billing, a destructive migration, row-level security or grants never merges by itself, and a turn that would commit a secret commits nothing. Only the owner's screen can turn it on or start it: the bridge, channels, guests and background work never do, and the main branch, a detached HEAD and force pushes are refused. (#1189)

name: v0.83.0
body:
### Fixed

- **The settings search finds the Claude bridge switch.** Searching "Claude", "bridge" or "operate" (in every language the app offers) now lands on the "Let Claude operate this app" switch and on full control, opening the Advanced block and moving focus to the switch. The other Advanced cards are indexed too, and the Security screen's bridge row offers "Turn on in Settings" when the bridge is off. Before, the search found nothing and the switch sat behind a closed block. (#1181)

### Added

- **A big task plans before it edits.** On the Code screen a request that names three or more files, or asks for a feature or a refactor (in English or Portuguese), now stops for a plan first: the agent proposes the files, the change in each, the tests and what stays out, and edits only after the owner approves; the approval card says the rule stopped it and why. "Plan first" is now Auto, Always or Never, a turn with nobody at the screen never waits on a plan, and the Claude bridge's `desktop_send` takes `plan_first`. The approved plan becomes the turn's checklist and survives compaction. (#1186)

- **A coding turn checks its own diff before it answers.** At the end of every Code-screen turn that changed something, a deterministic check reads the turn's diff and flags files the request never named (only when it names files), tests that were edited or removed and assertions that were loosened, scratch files left at the repo root, generated files edited without their source, and new CRLF line endings. The findings ride on the `done` frame as `self_check` and are added to the stored answer, so the next turn sees them; a check that could not measure says so instead of reporting clean. (#1185)

- **One test suite at a time per folder, and no job_status loops.** On the Code screen, a second test suite started in a folder where one is already running is refused with the running job's id and an instruction to wait, so pytest and vitest no longer fight over the same workspace; the folder is the effective one (`cd`, `--prefix`, `-C`). A foreground suite that outlives its timeout becomes a job instead of being lost. Asking `job_status` again with the same arguments now waits up to 30 s for news, and the Stop button cancels that wait, instead of burning a step per poll. The code prompt carries a short recipe: output to a file, the touched files' tests first, vitest with limited workers. (#1183)

- **Chimera Design opens from the Code bar, and the first click on an inactive artboard selects.** A "Chimera Design" button beside "Browse folder" opens the design list; before, only the command palette led there. Clicking an element of an inactive artboard now activates it and selects that element in one click, instead of needing a second click; a click on empty space selects nothing rather than bringing back the old selection. (#1182)

### Changed

- **A model nobody measured gets context in proportion to its window, and compaction restores the work.** A model without a measured useful context now compacts at half its window, capped at 128k tokens (64k when the window is unknown), instead of a fixed 64k for every model; a measured value still wins. After a compaction the next call carries the original request verbatim (bounded, with the cut named), the plan and task list, the files edited, and every command run with its exit code, including list-form commands and ones that timed out. (#1184)

name: v0.82.0
body:
### Fixed

- **A new worktree starts from the remote, not a stale local checkout.** Asking for a new worktree of a project now fetches and branches from the remote's default branch, says which commit it started from, and warns when it has to fall back to the local HEAD; the fetch never prompts for credentials. Before, a worktree could start days behind and the agent would work on old code without noticing. (#1173)

- **Files Chimera writes keep their line endings.** The agent's file writes went through a text mode that turned every newline into CRLF on Windows, so files it created disagreed with the repository and a translation hash passed on Windows and failed in CI; writes are now byte-exact, a new file gets LF, an existing CRLF file keeps CRLF, and translation hashes ignore line endings. (#1172)

- **A missing verify tool no longer marks a turn as failed.** When the check after a turn cannot run because its program is not installed in the checkout (say, `vitest` in a fresh worktree with no `node_modules`), the turn reads as not verified, with the reason and the fix (a `setup` command in `.chimera/verify.toml`), instead of failed; a check whose tests ran and failed still reads as failed. (#1170)

- **The test suite never calls a paid provider or leaks a key.** A text-to-speech test fell back to OpenRouter when a key was present, made a real paid call and wrote `speech.wav` into the repository; and gateways exporting a provider key left it in the environment for later tests. Both are isolated now. (#1169)

- **A failed memory extraction is no longer silent.** When the extraction behind a Code turn cannot start, the app now logs a warning naming the error type (never the conversation or a key), and the turn still answers. (#1168)

- **The installed app keeps its keys whatever folder it is opened from.** The backend read the `.env` of the folder the app was launched from and recorded that folder for the background service, so an app opened from a terminal elsewhere started with no provider key and every turn failed; the Start menu shortcut hid it. A packaged build now always runs its backend in the install folder. (#1167)

- **A number tweak applies when you finish typing.** The field applied on every key, so typing 34 into a tweak that runs from 28 to 56 sent 3 first, was refused and snapped back; it now applies once, on leaving the field or on Enter, clamps to the range, and Esc discards the draft. (#1166)

### Changed

- **The README no longer calls Chimera self-evolving.** Seven pre-registered learning runs found no measurable gain (`bench/learning_lift/RESULTS.md`), so the headline, the package description, the CLI help, the app and the translated READMEs and docs now say what the evidence supports: a governed agent that publishes its own null results. The translated READMEs also no longer promise an A/B test that the learning loop does not run. (#1171)

### Added

- **Chimera asks before working where commands are off.** A coding request in a folder whose commands are off now stops before any tool runs and asks the owner to allow them, continue without, or cancel; only the owner's screen can grant, a turn with nobody at the screen never waits, the choice is remembered per conversation, and an unverified answer says so at the top. Before, the agent could edit for an hour and only then say it could not check anything. (#1175)

- **The bridge pages and filters the conversation list.** Listing conversations through the Claude bridge returned all 1,465 at once (about 1 MB); it now takes `limit`, `cursor`, `state`, `project` and `q`, defaults to 50 per page on the bridge, and the screen's unparameterised list is unchanged. (#1174)

name: v0.81.0
body:
### Added

- **Images and fonts in HTML artboards.** Each design keeps its own store of images (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF) and fonts (WOFF2, WOFF, TTF), added from the assistant and kept once per content; screens and exports show them, the assistant knows which exist, and SVG and disguised files are refused. On the canvas they arrive as inline data, so the sandboxed screen still reaches no network. (#1163)

- **Named OpenAI-compatible endpoints.** `CHIMERA_ENDPOINTS` lists endpoints by name, base URL (https, or http on this machine) and the variable holding the key; a model written `endpoint/<name>/<model>` goes there with its own base and key, beside OpenRouter, instead of through the global `CHIMERA_API_BASE`. The privacy card, receipts and Usage name the endpoint and its host, and `/api/endpoints` lists and tests them. Part of #1133. (#1162)

- **A connector you name in a message connects for that turn.** With MCP autoload off, a Code turn whose message names a configured, enabled connector (say, "use the VoiceStudio connector") connects just that one, says so, and keeps it for later turns that name it; text from tools, pages or files never switches a connector on, and bots keep their own list. (#1161)

### Fixed

- **Code conversations no longer get cut in half.** Reopening a conversation rewrote its file in place, without a lock and from a read taken before a wait of up to ten seconds, so a reader or a crash in that window saw half a file and turns saved meanwhile were lost; under many parallel turns this damaged several sessions and their backups. Session writes are now atomic, flushed to disk and locked across processes, and the reopen merges only the fields it learned. (#1160)

- **HTML artboards use the design system's fonts, and each one opens its own inspector.** A token's font list was written as one quoted name, so screens fell back to a serif face on the canvas and in exports; and the inspector always showed the first artboard, so a second HTML screen could not reach its tweaks or select its elements. Clicking an artboard or its label now makes it the active one. (#1159)

- **Talking about Chimera Design while coding it no longer opens the canvas.** A message that names the product or asks for something visual is no longer read as a design request when it is plainly engineering work: a code path, a command such as pytest, or words like fix, implement or test. (#1158)

- **A URL connector's card describes what testing it does.** The detail of a connector reached by URL no longer says that testing starts a command or that npx may download a package, and a server on this machine (loopback) no longer carries the "reaches the network" chip. (#1157)

name: v0.80.0
body:
### Added

- **Skill card: do not widen types to silence the checker.** A new pattern card on narrowing a value or handling the missing branch instead of widening an annotation to `Any`, `object` or an unchecked union, translated into every site language. Contributed by @CG-5228. (#1150)

- **Design: watch an HTML artboard form while the model writes it.** A new proposal streams its page into a static preview as it is generated; the preview is sandboxed with no permissions, runs no script and reaches no network, and it gives way to the usual proposal, which is still applied only when you accept it. (#1154)

- **Design: tweaks and side-by-side directions for HTML artboards.** An artboard can declare typed CSS variables (colour, number, choice) that the inspector adjusts without calling the model, each change undoable and validated so no value can inject CSS; and the assistant can propose 2 to 4 distinct directions at once, laid out side by side and never applied until you accept. (#1153)

- **Design: fluid-width presentation and selection kept across reloads.** An HTML artboard with `mode: fill` now fills the screen in presentation (the canvas keeps its stored width, so zoom never triggers its media queries), and the selected element stays highlighted after the artboard reloads. (#1152)

- **Restricted model scripts in HTML artboards.** An HTML artboard may carry one model-written `text/x-chimera` script that runs only on the canvas, in an opaque-origin frame whose CSP admits that block by hash; thumbnails and exports stay script-free. (#1151)

- **Export HTML artboards.** HTML artboards now export to HTML, PDF, PNG and PPTX; the PPTX keeps each text block editable, and every export renders with scripts and network off. (#1149)

- **Edit an HTML artboard element in place.** In Chimera Design, clicking an element of an HTML artboard selects it, and the inspector changes its inline style and text without a model call; each change undoes exactly, and the selection reaches the model as fenced data. (#1148)

- **Chimera Design draws screens as HTML/CSS.** The design agent now writes each artboard as a self-contained HTML/CSS screen, rendered in a sandboxed frame on the canvas; the piece-by-piece operations remain for fine adjustments. (#1147)

- **The design agent can write HTML artboards.** New `write_artboard`, `edit_artboard` and `read_artboard` actions write one screen at a time and revise by exact replacement instead of rewriting the file; design tokens become CSS variables. (#1145)

- **HTML artboards render on the design canvas.** An artboard with an HTML source shows on the canvas, in thumbnails and in presentation inside a fully sandboxed frame with its own content security policy; design tokens become CSS variables. (#1144)

- **Chimera Design artboards can hold an HTML/CSS source.** The first step toward generating each screen as HTML: a validated, allowlisted source per artboard with exact-undo operations. (#1143)

### Fixed

- **The desktop updater no longer ships a vulnerable `zip`.** The updater unpacks Windows updates with `zip`, which moves from 4.6.1 to 9.1.3 and past three advisories: a critical header differential that can overwrite arbitrary files, unbounded symlink targets that can exhaust memory, and an AES authentication bypass. An update was only unpacked after its signature verified, which limited the exposure. (#1156)

name: Chimera 0.79.1
body:
Chimera 0.79.1

## [0.79.1] - 2026-10-28
### Fixed

- **Approving a design no longer fails with "another Chimera process asked this question".** The design approval is answered as a question in its conversation, in the approvals window, the status bar and the Governance list. Only the owner's screen can answer it, and two answers at once record exactly one. (#1139)

- **Chimera Design gets a usable first proposal.** A malformed operation comes back as an argument error the model can fix, each operation shows its shape, a cut-off proposal is detected and asked again with fewer operations, and the first proposal asks for typography, backgrounds and shapes instead of plain text. (#1140)

- **Connectors start on Windows, and the app opens without waiting for them.** A connector whose command passes through a Windows `.cmd` launcher (Supabase through `npx`) no longer breaks on an `&` in its URL; an argument that can't pass safely is refused with the reason. The service opens at once and connects the MCP servers in the background, instead of keeping the app on "Failed to fetch" for up to two minutes. (#1138)

- **Audio and images from connectors arrive as files, not as text the model has to read.** A connector that returns a recording or a picture inline (VoiceStudio's narration, for one) used to fill the model's context with base64 and stop the turn. The file is now saved in the project's `mcp-output/` folder, kept out of commits, and the conversation can play or show it. (#1137)

### Security

- **litellm moves past a security advisory.** The model gateway library is now 1.105.6, out of the range of a high-severity advisory about its proxy server. Chimera uses it as a library, so it was unlikely to be exposed. (#1136)

### Added

- **"Ignore permissions" per project, kept across restarts.** A project's switch covers all its conversations, including new ones; each conversation keeps its own switch too. Turning it on releases the cards already waiting. After a restart a banner names each saved project and conversation and reactivates the ones you confirm with one click; the rest are discarded. Only the desktop screen can turn it on, and turning it off always applies. (#1141)

name: Chimera 0.79.0
body:
Chimera 0.79.0

## [0.79.0] - 2026-10-27
### Added

- **Connect VoiceStudio in one click.** Settings › Connectors lists "VoiceStudio (local)", a local voice studio (cloning, voice design, speech, transcription). The card connects when VoiceStudio is running and says how to install it when it isn't. It names the non-commercial default voice model and the need for consent before cloning a voice. (#1134)

- **Speech, music and video through OpenRouter.** With only an OpenRouter key, the agent can now narrate text (`text_to_speech`), make music or sound effects (`generate_audio`), and make short videos (`generate_video`). `generate_image` reports what each image cost. (#1130)

### Changed

- **"Ignore permissions" covers turns sent through the desktop bridge.** When you turn it on for a conversation on the screen, turns another tool sends into that conversation through the desktop bridge no longer stop for approval. Paired devices and plain API tokens still do, and only the screen can switch the mode. (#1132)

- **A calmer Code screen.** A finished turn shows a short receipt (tool calls, failures, files, server, media, verification) with "show all" for the rest, and big diffs fold. The header keeps what matters and puts every other action in a "⋯" menu. On narrow windows the side panel becomes a drawer. (#1131)

### Fixed

- **Tidier settings and project list.** Usage names runs without a recorded model instead of showing a dash, the Usage, Security and Decisions pages line up with the rest, the project list shows each existing folder once and can remove one, Tasks shows project names, and a schedule whose folder is gone says so. (#1128)

- **Workspace media plays in the conversation.** Audio and video the agent wrote get a player that loads on press, relative image paths show the picture, images are capped in height, the HTML preview uses the full height of its panel, and "Mais recentes" reaches the end of a long conversation. (#1127)

- **Fewer approval cards after a browser hiccup, and the design skill loads again.** A browser action that failed before reading a page no longer marks the turn as having read untrusted content, so harmless commands afterwards stop asking for approval. Reading a skill by name (`skill_view`) no longer fails on every call. (#1126)

- **An approval card no longer outlives the question.** A card whose asking process died (an update, a restart) stayed on screen until a 24-hour sweep, and Refuse could not clear it. A question now leaves the list once its own wait has ended, and an answer to it is not recorded. (#1125)

Also in this release: a `changelog_digest` workflow recipe in `examples/` (#1092, thanks @CG-5228).

name: Chimera 0.78.2
body:
Chimera 0.78.2

## [0.78.2] - 2026-10-27
### Added

- **SVG images are accepted, after validation.** Vector models such as Recraft V4.1 Vector return SVG; Chimera rebuilds it from an allowlist (no scripts, event handlers, external links or entity declarations), saves it as `.svg`, and serves it with a sandboxing Content-Security-Policy. (#1115)

### Changed

- **Google search in your own Chrome follows "Ignore permissions".** With the switch on, searches in the paired, visible Chrome run without a card, still paced (one every 20 s, 30 a day) and stopped at a CAPTCHA. When every search key is out of credit or refused, `web_search` tells the agent to use the browser's Google search instead. (#1116)

### Fixed

- generate_image reports OpenRouter's upstream image errors instead of "no image", names the replacement for the retired gpt-image-1 and gpt-5-image ids, and asks Gemini for a square image. (#1123)

- A browser navigation that failed before any page loaded (for example, a site not yet granted to the Chrome extension) no longer marks the turn as having read untrusted content. (#1122)

- The Chrome extension works on current Chrome again: the download denial no longer fails every action with "Cannot access browser-level commands" (downloads are cancelled by a guard instead), Cancel on Chrome's debugging bar can be undone with "Resume Chimera actions" in the popup, and the popup stops offering Allow for a site already granted. (#1121)

- The deepseek-v4-flash catalogue row reads 0.14 in, the live OpenRouter price, so the cost shown for it is not understated. (#1120)

- Registering the Chrome host checks that its Python can read the OS vault (keyring) and refuses with the exact install command when it cannot; before, the extension stayed "paired, disconnected" with no reason given. (#1119)

- Google search in the paired Chrome works: the extension only attaches to web pages in its own tab group (a group tab left on a `chrome://` page made every action fail with "Cannot access a chrome:// URL"), and the results page is recorded by its URL, so trusted sources apply to it. (#1118)

- The Chrome extension pairing survives desktop app updates: the browser host accepts the app's service from any version folder of its own `service-bin`, instead of only the exact version it was registered with. (#1117)

name: Chimera 0.78.1
body:
Chimera 0.78.1

## [0.78.1] - 2026-10-26
### Fixed

- **Image-only models work through OpenRouter.** FLUX, Recraft, GPT Image and Krea go to OpenRouter's images endpoint with the size parameters each model declares; before, every one of them failed instantly with a bare "image generation failed". Failures now say why (HTTP status and OpenRouter's message). (#1113)

- **The "Ignore permissions" button shows its state and acts at once.** It always read "off" because the conversation list never carried the switch, and turning it on mid-turn only took effect on the next turn. The button now shows the real state, and the running turn's next action is released as soon as the switch is on. (#1112)

- Web search says why it failed: a refused key, an account out of credit (top up at the provider) or a failing provider, and the `auto` mode moves on to the next configured provider instead of retrying a dead one. (#1111)

- A run whose model provider and fallback both time out now ends with a record (cost of the calls already made, reason "provider_timeout", exit code 13) instead of crashing with nothing written. (#1110)

name: Chimera 0.78.0
body:
Chimera 0.78.0

## [0.78.0] - 2026-10-26
### Added

- **Chimera Design draws as the agent works.** The canvas applies the agent's changes batch by batch instead of reloading the whole design, falls back to a full reload when a batch is missing or fails, and shows "Creating…" while the agent draws. (#1107)

- Chimera Design: a title menu (rename, duplicate, export), a share link that opens the design, hand, frame and note tools, zoom as a menu, a full-screen Present mode, and phone, tablet and desktop previews. (#1106)

- **The agent makes images with your OpenRouter key, and you see them in the conversation.** `generate_image` now works with OpenRouter's image models (`CHIMERA_IMAGE_MODEL`, default `google/gemini-3.1-flash-image`) and no longer needs an OpenAI key. Each image is saved to `generated_images/` in the project and appears in the answer. An image a model returns in the middle of a turn is kept instead of lost. Choosing an image model that cannot use tools as the conversation's model no longer fails. The agent can also look at an image it made, when its model has vision. (#1105)

- **Trusted sources.** The owner can list sites (or `*` for every public site) whose content does not restrict the run afterwards, so reading the web no longer turns every later command into an approval. Mail, MCP output and local addresses still count as untrusted. (#1103)

- Chimera Design: the agent submits a design for approval in the conversation (approve, or ask for changes with a note), and project code waits until the current version is approved. (#1102)

- Chimera Design: designs with several screens get an index page generated from the artboards, links between screens, and navigation in the canvas and the preview. (#1101)

- Chimera Design: comments anchored to the canvas, with threads you can resolve, a Comments panel that jumps to the element, and the agent reads the open comments and resolves them when addressed. (#1095)

- **Chimera Design now works like a designer at your side.** When you ask for a visual design, the agent first says what it is going for (concept, palette, typography), lists its plan as a checklist that updates as it goes, and builds the design screen by screen. It does not touch your project's code until you approve the design. The design opens beside the conversation as soon as the agent starts it, the card in the conversation opens it with one click, and the tool list says what happened ("Design: updated"). (#1090)

### Changed

- **"Ignore permissions" now releases every connection.** With the switch on, the agent works directly with git, GitHub, `gh`, MCP connectors (Hostinger, Supabase and others), deploys, uploads and send tools. It still asks before destructive commands, before reading or sending a secret file, and before rewriting the main branch. Listing the MCP servers no longer marks the run as untrusted. (#1104)

### Fixed

- Continuing a conversation right after stopping its turn no longer runs the new turn in the app's default folder instead of the conversation's worktree. That mistake turned every read and edit in the worktree into an "outside the project folder" approval. (#1100)

- **The "Ignore permissions" button in the Code screen works.** Clicking it did nothing: the request was refused, and the screen did not say so. It now turns the mode on and off for the conversation, its label shows which way it is set, and a failure is shown instead of swallowed. (#1094)

- The vitest cache file is no longer tracked, and `node_modules/` is ignored at any level, so running the desktop tests from the repo root no longer dirties the worktree. (#1093)

- **On Linux with the built-in sandbox, a running command can be stopped and its output shows as it comes.** Before, cancelling a command run inside the bubblewrap sandbox did nothing, and its output appeared only when it finished. (#1091)

- **The Tools screen describes the pull-request tool in every language.** Its description was missing from the translations. The tests that guard those descriptions also no longer give a different answer depending on whether the machine running them has the tool switched on. (#1089)

name: Chimera 0.77.0
body:
Chimera 0.77.0

## [0.77.0] - 2026-10-25
### Fixed

- **The desktop app's background service no longer gets stuck half-stopped.** A messaging adapter that had never connected (for example a Discord bot with a wrong token) made the service's shutdown fail partway. The service then stayed running without answering, and the app could not reach it until the process was ended by hand. Each shutdown step now runs on its own, and the service always exits. (#1086)

- **The agent's questions reach you even when it phrases the call loosely.** A question sent with both a heading and a list of questions used to be refused with an error that did not say what to change, and the agent could retry the same call a dozen times without the question ever reaching the screen. The list of questions is now asked, and the extra heading no longer makes the call fail. (#1084)

- **A reply cut off mid-tool-call no longer ends the turn with half a project.** The call that could not be read goes back to the model with a request to retry it. Removing the Tailwind or PostCSS setup from a critical config file (next, postcss, tailwind, vite) is now flagged for review, a project with only a build script is verified by running that build, a project's model now applies in its subfolders, `chimera run -` reads non-ASCII input correctly on Windows, and the background service reserves far less memory. (#1082)

### Changed

- **Claude models now use the prompt cache, so long turns cost far less.** Every call path marks the stable part of the conversation, including the latest tool result, so each step rereads the previous one from the provider's cache instead of paying for it again. It is on by default for Claude models; `CHIMERA_PROMPT_CACHE=0` turns it off. (#1083)

### Added

- **The agent can check a page at phone width before calling it done.** A new browser action measures whether the page scrolls sideways at 375 px (or another width) and names the elements that overflow. It also reports whether the page's CSS actually loaded, so a site that lost its styles is no longer reported as finished. (#1087)

- **The agent can look at the app it is building.** When a Code turn starts a dev server in the background inside the project folder, its browser may open that server's port, and only that one. Reading a page served entirely from that port no longer makes later commands ask for approval; a page that loads anything from elsewhere, or opens a connection elsewhere, is treated as before. Chimera's own ports and other local ports stay closed. (#1085)

name: v0.76.0
body:
## [0.76.0] - 2026-10-24
### Fixed

- **Claude models work in the Code screen again.** With an Anthropic model as the default, every coding turn failed on its first step with an error about a tool's input schema. The question tool's schema used a construct Anthropic's API refuses; it is now a plain object, and a test checks every tool's schema so the problem cannot come back. (#1077)

### Added

- **Each project can have its own model.** A Code conversation uses its own pinned model, then the project's, then the global default, and the turn's receipt says which one was used. Changing the model for one project no longer changes it for conversations in another. When the agent proposes a different model, it can only leave you a card naming the conversation or project it would apply to; nothing changes until you approve it. (#1078)
